title: Best Book Interior Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a book interior designer for print and ebook formatting: what to include, how to prepare, price factors and red flags.
intro: Book design, also called interior formatting or typesetting, turns a manuscript into pages that are comfortable to read in print and as an ebook. It covers fonts, margins, chapter openings, headers and page numbers. Poor formatting makes even a great book look amateur and can cause files to be rejected by printers and ebook stores. This guide helps you get a professional interior.

faq.q: What is the difference between print and ebook formatting?
faq.a: Print layouts have fixed pages, margins and page numbers. Ebooks usually reflow text to fit any screen. Each needs its own file, often a print-ready PDF and an EPUB.

faq.q: When should I order book design?
faq.a: After editing and proofreading are finished. Changing text after layout is slow and can shift every page.

faq.q: What trim size should I choose?
faq.a: It depends on your genre and printer. Common sizes are listed by print-on-demand services; your designer can recommend one.

faq.q: Can the designer add images and tables?
faq.a: Yes, but they add work. Mention them in the brief so the quote is accurate.

faq.q: Will the files meet my platform's requirements?
faq.a: They should. Share your printer or platform's specifications, and ask the designer to confirm the files pass their checks.
